dedupe_keys.name: iiot vulnset vulnerabilities and attacks in industrial iot protocols unsw canberra

description: IIoT-VulnSet is a dataset for vulnerability assessment in Industrial Internet of Things environments. The IEEE DataPort page says a testbed of interconnected virtual machines and simulated IIoT environments was built at UNSW Canberra (ADFA campus) to emulate an industrial network, a range of cyber attacks was launched to exploit vulnerabilities in several industrial protocols, and the data link each attack vector to the exploited protocol vulnerability; formats are AVI, CSV, TXT and ZIP. It was submitted by Ahmed Aldysty, Nour Moustafa and Erandi Lakshika of the School of Systems and Computing, UNSW Canberra, and last updated on 7 July 2026, as one zip of about 10.8 GB. The page grants free use for academic research and requires the author's permission for commercial use, while DataCite lists CC BY 4.0; it is a Standard Dataset, so files need an IEEE DataPort subscription (US$40 a month, free for IEEE Society members). Coverage is one virtual testbed. Caveats: the protocols covered are not named in the part of the page read, and the environment is fully virtual. For simulation it gives attack-to-vulnerability links to set how likely each protocol weakness is exploited in cyber risk models of plants. Related catalogue records include X-IIoTID and the ICS advisories architectural weaknesses dataset.
